To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DDX3 promotes neural crest induction and cranio facial morphogenesis through the activation of AKT signaling.
DDX3 promotes NC induction by regulating the activity of the AKT kinase.
the RNA helicases DDX3 and RAC1 promote neural crest development by regulating AKT activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how cells communicate to each other during development, and the role of RNA helicase in these cellular communications.
the mechanisms of craniofacial development and the molecular mechanisms that cause birth defects.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of the craniofacial region and the neural crest, a population of embryonic cells that give rise to a wide variety of adult tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DDX3 promotes NC induction and cranial neural crest development in part by promoting AKT/GSK3β/β-catenin/Snai1 signaling, and this is mediated by RAC.
DDX3 regulates AKT activity during NC induction by promoting translation of the small GTPase RAC1, and that this regulation is critical for NC development.
DDX3 regulates neural crest development by promoting AKTAKT activity, which in turn regulates β-catenin, GSK3β and Snai1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DDX3 regulates AKT activity and NC induction by promoting RAC1 translation.
the RNA helicases DDX3 and RAC1 are required to induce the neural crest in Xenopus by promoting AKT signaling and the subsequent inhibition of GSK3B activity.
DDX3 regulates NC development by promoting the AKT pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DDX3 regulates NC development by promoting the translation and function of RAC1, an important regulator of AKT signaling.
DDX3 regulates NC development by promoting the activity of AKT.
